solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Hang up over hint of sarcasm in dispatch

indicators.note: in says the next build is placed inside the word for dispatch

parts.note: to dispatch a letter is to send it

indicators.note: over here means covering, so the word up is wrapped around the single letter

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: a hint of a word is just its opening letter

explanation.surface: Someone slams down the phone after detecting a trace of sarcasm in a message.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hang up' looks like the whole definition, but 'up' belongs to the wordplay. 'over' here means covering, not on top, and 'in' gives the outer layer.
explanation.definitionFit: To hang something is to suspend it, letting it dangle from a support above.

clue.text: Maybe Mr M'Choakumchild shocked her with chocolates

indicators.note: shocked suggests something jolted out of order, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: A man startles a woman by giving her chocolates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shocked' rearranges HER with CHOCOLATES. Mr M'Choakumchild is the fact-cramming schoolmaster in Dickens's Hard Times.
explanation.definitionFit: Dickens's character runs a classroom, so he is an example of a teacher in a school.

clue.text: Set in motion by leading sheep

parts.note: a star plays the leading role
a tup is a ram, a male sheep

explanation.surface: A flock is driven forward by the animal at the front.
explanation.walkthrough: TUP is a dialect word for a ram.
explanation.definitionFit: To get something going is to launch it, an idiom for beginning an operation.

clue.text: Contributing to success enjoyed by City

indicators.note: Contributing to says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A town's prosperity is credited to a contribution.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition 'by City' is narrowed to 'City': 'by' is a link word and cannot stand in for a city's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Essen is an industrial city in Germany's Ruhr region.

clue.text: No longer important to avoid as it's defunct

definitions.note: an adjective, used for the noun phrase as in saying it is a lost cause

parts.note: an issue that is dead no longer matters
to duck a question is to avoid it

explanation.surface: Something past mattering is best avoided because it no longer works.
explanation.definitionFit: A plan with no chance of success is a failure beyond reviving, a lost cause.

clue.text: Unable to think clearly when charged first off

indicators.note: first off asks for the opening letter of the synonym to be dropped

parts.note: to be charged with a burden is to be saddled with it

explanation.surface: Someone facing a criminal charge is too flustered to think straight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first off' takes the S from SADDLED.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone confused or muddled in the head is said to be befuddled in this way.

clue.text: Witness form being overturned in a race

indicators.note: in places the turned word inside the other pieces

parts.note: the TT is the Tourist Trophy motorcycle race on the Isle of Man

indicators.note: being overturned in a down clue means the word is turned upside down

parts.note: a set, like a form, is a class grouping pupils in school

explanation.surface: An onlooker sees a document capsized during a race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being overturned' turns SET into TES, which goes 'in' A plus TT.
explanation.definitionFit: To witness a signature formally is to confirm or certify it, a legal sense.

clue.text: Criticise record of Nonconformist

parts.note: diss is slang for criticise or disrespect
to enter data is to record it

explanation.surface: Someone finds fault with the history of a dissident churchgoer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'record' looks like a noun; here it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A Nonconformist is a Protestant outside the Church of England, a dissenter from its doctrine.

clue.text: Not initially expensive to get standard form of ID

indicators.note: not initially means the opening letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: dear means expensive
a mark is a standard, as in up to the mark

explanation.surface: It costs a lot to get an ordinary identity document.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not initially' removes the D from DEAR.
explanation.definitionFit: An earmark is an identifying notch or tag on a farm animal's ear.

clue.text: An advantage being the principal's floozy

parts.note: the principal of a school is its head, so the principal's is head's
tart is a slang word for a floozy

explanation.surface: A cynical remark that having an affair with the head teacher gives you a leg up.
explanation.definitionFit: A start given before others in a race is a lead, a benefit you get before the contest begins.

clue.text: Cancel fight

definitions.meaning: to cancel a plan is to drop or abandon it

explanation.surface: An order to call off a bout.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: abandoning a scheme, and a brief scuffle between people.

clue.text: Talk foolishly about cast-iron resolve causing delay

indicators.note: about means the talking word goes around the other letters

parts.note: to prate is to talk foolishly at length

indicators.note: resolve read as re-solve says the letters are worked out afresh in another order

explanation.surface: Idle chatter about firm determination ends in putting things off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resolve' is read as re-solve, giving OCRASTIN, and 'about' wraps the talk around it; 'causing' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Putting off a task again and again is postponing it.

clue.text: Against accepting return of books on Russia's foremost dramatist

indicators.note: accepting means the word for against takes the next letters into its middle

parts.note: on can mean against, as in leaning on a wall

indicators.note: on in an across clue means the books come after the Russian letter
the foremost letter of a word is its first
return of means the abbreviation for books is read backwards

parts.note: OT is the Old Testament, a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A list of objections to a famous Russian playwright's book list.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue 'on' means placed after, so the turned books (from 'return of') follow R; 'accepting' then encloses the lot. OT, the Old Testament, is the usual crossword 'books'.
explanation.definitionFit: Joe Orton was an English playwright of the 1960s, author of Loot and Entertaining Mr Sloane.

clue.text: Weapon lacking bit of accuracy carried by extremely old outlaw

indicators.note: carried by means the shortened weapon sits inside the word for extremely

parts.note: dead is slang for extremely, as in dead easy

indicators.note: lacking means a letter is taken out of the weapon word

parts.note: a spear is a thrown or thrust weapon

indicators.note: a bit of a word here is its first letter

explanation.surface: An ancient outlaw's spear is described as missing its accuracy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking' leaves SPER, which 'carried by' places inside the slang 'dead', as in dead right.
explanation.definitionFit: A desperado is a reckless criminal, the classic bandit of the Wild West.

clue.text: To surpass Nick is superb

parts.note: to top something is to surpass it
a nick is a small cut or notch

explanation.surface: Someone praises the achievement of beating a rival named Nick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nick' looks like a man's name; it is a small cut.
explanation.definitionFit: Something first-rate is of the highest quality, an informal synonym for excellent.

clue.text: Exaggerate about involving government

parts.note: over can mean about, as in arguing over money
state as an adjective means run by government, as in state schools

explanation.surface: Someone is accused of overplaying matters concerning those in power.
explanation.definitionFit: To say more than the facts justify is to overplay or inflate a claim.

clue.text: Novelist and rector associated with somewhere in the Midlands

indicators.note: associated with joins the two pieces, the town's name coming before the clergyman's letter

parts.note: Stoke-on-Trent is a city in the English Midlands

explanation.surface: A literary figure and a clergyman are linked to a town in central England.
explanation.walkthrough: STOKE is Stoke-on-Trent, a pottery city in the English Midlands.
explanation.definitionFit: Bram Stoker was the Irish writer of Dracula.

clue.text: Moved stealthily ignoring son on speed of bear

indicators.note: on in a down clue puts the first piece above the second
ignoring means the abbreviation for son is left out

parts.note: stole is the past tense of steal, to creep quietly
rate means speed

explanation.surface: An animal creeps along without its cub at a bear's pace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ignoring son' removes S from STOLE, leaving TOLE. 'bear' looks like the animal but means put up with.
explanation.definitionFit: To bear something is to endure or put up with it.

clue.text: Helping to make fragrant herb a producer of pollen

indicators.note: Helping to make says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A sweet-smelling plant contributes to the making of pollen.
explanation.definitionFit: In a flower, the anther is the part of the stamen where pollen grains form.

clue.text: Start of impeachment interrupting president at height of success

indicators.note: interrupting means the letter breaks into the president's name

parts.note: Donald Trump was US president

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Impeachment proceedings begin against a president at the peak of his power.
explanation.walkthrough: Written in 2019, when Trump's first impeachment was under way.
explanation.definitionFit: A triumph is a great victory or achievement.

clue.text: Fellow socialists finding established standards embraced by Mr Attlee at first? Just the opposite

indicators.note: embraced by would put the standards inside the name, but the clue then reverses that
just the opposite flips the containment, so the standards embrace the name instead

parts.note: codes are established standards of conduct or practice
taken as written

indicators.note: at first takes only the opening letter of the surname

explanation.surface: Party colleagues find that the norms were once adopted by the Labour leader Clement Attlee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'embraced by' with 'Just the opposite' means CODES embraces MR plus A (Attlee's first letter). Attlee was the British Labour Prime Minister from 1945 to 1951.
explanation.definitionFit: Socialists traditionally address one another as comrade, a word for a fellow member or ally.

clue.text: Make out with Cockney girl after record comes to an end

indicators.note: after places the girl's word behind the record

parts.note: a disc is a gramophone record
her, with the h dropped as in a Cockney accent

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A London girl gets amorous once the record finishes.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockneys, working-class Londoners, drop their h's, so 'her' becomes 'ER. 'comes to' links N, the end of 'an'. 'Make out' looks like kissing but means perceive.
explanation.definitionFit: To make something out is to perceive it, managing to see or understand it.

clue.text: American tucking into some fancy dessert

indicators.note: tucking into means the abbreviation goes inside the other letters
fancy as an adjective means elaborate, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An American eats some elaborate pudding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tucking into' looks like eating, but it is a containment signal; 'fancy' gives MOSE to hold the American.
explanation.definitionFit: A mousse is a light, airy pudding of whipped cream or egg whites.

clue.text: This alone surprisingly produces frozen rain

indicators.note: surprisingly says the letters of these words turn up in an unexpected order

explanation.surface: A remark that one thing is enough to create icy precipitation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surprisingly' rearranges THIS ALONE.
explanation.definitionFit: A pellet of ice falling from storm clouds is a form of frozen precipitation.

clue.text: We object over small trace of helicobacter discovered on bottom of Petri dish

indicators.note: over means the pronoun is turned backwards

parts.note: the object form of the pronoun we is us

indicators.note: a trace of a word is its first letter
the bottom of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: Scientists protest after a stomach bug is found in a lab culture plate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns US into SU. Helicobacter is a stomach bacterium; 'dish' looks part of the Petri dish but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Sushi is a Japanese dish of vinegared rice topped or rolled with raw fish.

clue.text: Head of science reluctant to disregard absolute laziness

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter
to disregard means the letter for absolute is left out

parts.note: loath means reluctant

explanation.surface: A senior scientist is unwilling to ignore idleness altogether.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing A leaves LOTH, itself a variant spelling of loath.
explanation.definitionFit: Sloth is idleness, one of the seven deadly sins.

clue.text: Dance club falling short on drink

indicators.note: on joins the shortened club after the drink

parts.note: rum is a spirit

indicators.note: falling short means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a bat is a club used in sport

explanation.surface: A dance venue running out of supplies relies on alcohol.
explanation.walkthrough: 'falling short' cuts BAT to BA.
explanation.definitionFit: The rumba is a Cuban ballroom dance.

clue.text: Cleaner having time after work for Corrie perhaps

indicators.note: after places the word for time behind the word for work

parts.note: soap is a cleaning agent
op is short for opus, a musical work
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: A cleaner takes a break after work to watch television.
explanation.walkthrough: Corrie is Coronation Street, a long-running British TV serial set in a Manchester street.
explanation.definitionFit: Coronation Street is an example of a long-running serial drama on television.

clue.text: Knock off bag

definitions.meaning: knock off is slang for steal
to bag something can mean to take it for yourself, to pinch it

explanation.surface: An instruction to steal a handbag.
explanation.definitionFit: Both slang phrases mean to steal or pinch something.

clue.text: Increase in Parisian Chinese seen at church

parts.note: en is French for in
the Han are China's majority ethnic group
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A Chinese person in Paris is spotted at a church service.
explanation.definitionFit: To improve or heighten something is to boost its quality or value.
